text:
sam (sales): @mariana we just heard from ORION Pay — go-live is T+1 (24h). Their stress run shows our admission control is throttling them hard in us-west-2. They need a quota bump (GPU concurrency + soft rate limit) for a 6h window. Can infra do a temp override? :pray:
mariana (infra): Sam — what's the model + expected peak RPS and concurrency? FYI the us-west-2 GPU pool is at 92% overall and we've been seeing queue length spikes this afternoon (~280 queued requests). Tail gen latency ~750ms. Link to dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/cluster/us-west-2 (logs + traces there).
akshay (eng): If they're hitting admission, it's probably the per-customer concurrency cap + global pool saturation. We have three levers: 1) temp concurrency bump for the customer, 2) prioritized project queueing, 3) route some traffic to smaller model variants.
jessica (support): I can gather ORION's exact RPS and concurrency from their SRE contact now. Sam, can you confirm the expected sustained RPS for the launch window?
sam (sales): They expect ~120 rps bursty, ~60 sustained, model family: gpt-xxl-8k (quantized), concurrency around 40. They prefer not to change model for launch.
mariana (infra): Ok — options: A) Emergency override: increase per-customer GPU concurrency to 60 in us-west-2 for 6 hours. Risk: may push other tenants' queueing and increase tail latency. B) Prioritized queue: tag ORION as priority for routing (works if we can accept partial fairness). C) Ask them to route non-critical traffic to a smaller model.
sales-ops: Any cost implications if we do A? We need to quote the uplift to ORION.
mariana (infra): There is a cost uplift since we'll reserve burst capacity and risk preemption for lower tiers. Rough estimate: +25% token/unit for the window. Also we'll bill a one-off override charge to their invoice.
akshay (eng): Implementation is trivial via control plane CLI. Example (will be gated by ops auth):
```
# apply temporary concurrency override for ORION
redwoodctl quota set --customer ORION_PAY --region us-west-2 --gpu-concurrency 60 --duration 6h --reason "launch override"
```
On success it updates admission-controller and the routing table. We'll need oncall to apply.
oncall-bot: ALERT: k8s pod queue length > 200 in us-west-2 (metric window 5m). Current pool utilization: 92%.
mariana (infra): I'm concerned about moving the needle on global SLOs. Akshay, can we apply prioritized queueing scope-limited to ORION so it doesn't exceed a hard cap?
akshay (eng): Yes — we can set a dynamic priority with a hard cap: priority weight = high, hard concurrency cap = 60. That keeps a ceiling.
jessica (support): Sam — I'll need the customer's billing contact to sign the override T&Cs (cost uplift + duration). Please drop contact here.
sam (sales): Billing contact: taylor@orionpay.com. They approved the uplift verbally, will sign doc.
mariana (infra): Plan: if sales ops approves, oncall will run the CLI snippet and set cap=60 for 6h with a scheduled rollback. I'll monitor queues and rollback early if we see cross-tenant SLO violations. Can ops confirm?
sales-ops: Confirmed — approve one-time override. We'll create a PO and send T&Cs to ORION.
oncall-bot: ACTION by oncall user @marc: starting override request ticket #INC-17542.
mariana (infra): @marc please apply override at 02:00 UTC tomorrow and post the apply timestamp here. Also enable verbose tracing for ORION for the window.
marc (oncall): applying override now (scheduled). CLI shows success. Override applied at 1754204000. Monitoring: queued requests dropped from 280 -> 45 within 120s, tail latency down to 420ms.
sam (sales): Awesome, thanks everyone — will confirm with ORION after launch. :tada:
mariana (infra): Leaving this thread open for post-launch telemetry. If queueing resurfaces we'll revert and pursue longer-term capacity add in us-west-2.
